doc.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: What counts as jazz: ECM and improvisation
summary: ECM includes improvisers who are not strictly jazz; he sees himself as a jazz guitarist who also plays non-jazz.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: But then when you find musicians, I think especially more and more now you find European musicians who go back to their roots, go back to the music of their country, they try to incorporate the music of Norway or Sweden or wherever they happen to be coming from, I mean, into jazz. And then you have other people that record for ECM that I mean there’s this wonderful oud player named Anouar Brahem, I’m not sure if I’m pronouncing it right, but he doesn’t play jazz at all, he plays oud. But he improvises you know. And he did an album with Dave Holland, it’s wonderful. But then again you start to raise the other question, well what is jazz. Yeah I mean a lot of what’s on ECM I wouldn’t consider coming from a pure strain of jazz at all but it’s coming from the spirit of it which has to do with a lot of improvising. And that’s one of the aspects of jazz that can take it away from being the pure form of jazz which has to do with blues and African-American music and what the Ken Burns show presented, which is definitely true, and I really believe in that. There’s a pure strain of jazz. But then there’s something else. There’s jazz influence and inspired and that’s improvisation and I think maybe you don’t quite call it jazz in the pure sense, but it’s jazz in the spirit of what the music is and I think there’s a lot of disservice when they don’t talk about that kind of music because there’s some great improvisers who don’t play in the jazz tradition you know. I happen to be kind of caught in the whole, I’m walking funny lines because I mean I really consider I’m a jazz guitar player but I also like to play things that sound nothing like jazz. And it doesn’t bother me at all you know. I don’t feel like I’m breaking the rules you know.
